newsitem.title: MEXICO: At least 12 injured in Mexico City fuel blast.
newsitem.headline: At least 12 injured in Mexico City fuel blast.

text.p: At least 12 people were injured on Monday when a fuel storage tank owned by state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) exploded in a suburb of Mexico City, witnesses and officials said.

A dense cloud of thick, black smoke rose thousands of feet (metres) into the air from the site of the explosion and was visible from virtually all points of the capital as the fire raged out of control.
"We have admitted six patients," a doctor at the Magdalena de las Salinas hospital said, adding they were suffering from second- and third-degree burns.
The Mexican Red Cross said another six people had been taken to other hospitals, according to government news agency Notimex.
Authorities evacuated people from the surrounding area as scores of ambulances, fire trucks and army units rushed to the scene.
The explosion at the 18,000 liter tank occurred at 3:05 p.m. (2105 GMT) at Pemex's storage and distribution center in the industrial suburb of San Juan Ixhuatepec.
Radio station Radio Red said between 14 and 25 people had been injured. A TV Azteca report that one person had died could not be immediately confirmed.
There was no immediate official comment from Petroleos Mexicanos, the state oil and gas monopoly.
Witnesses said firefighters were spraying jets of water on four adjoining fuel tanks to try to stop the huge fire started by the explosion from spreading.
TV Azteca said local residents had been pressing for some time for the storage depot to be relocated because of safety concerns.
The San Juan district, known as San Juanico, was the site of a huge gas explosion 12 years ago which killed hundreds of people.

The explosion was the second in recent months at a Pemex installation. On July 26 a blast caused by human error at the firm's Cactus gas processing center in the southern state of Chiapas killed six workers.
